name: Mama Cassavir, “the Switchboard”
meet: her shuttered transit exchange on the upper Flats
pays: clean ¥ through her exchange, minus her cut
pitch: Cassavir calls from the switchboard with a job she vouches for.
Cassavir has a client who needs discreet professionals, and she named the crew.
Cassavir is calling in a favor — and paying for it anyway.

name: a Nyx Churn broker
meet: a drifting stall in the Churn
pays: cash chips, no questions — and a favor owed to Nyx
pitch: A Churn broker speaking for Nyx has a job and doesn’t want anyone asking why.
Nyx’s people have a problem they’d rather someone else be seen solving.
The Churn is paying double, which means the job is worth triple to somebody.

name: an anonymous corp cut-out
meet: a rented executive booth in a Grid noodle arcade
pays: ¥ in escrow, half up front, plus corp scrip
pitch: A cut-out in a good suit represents a conglomerate that will never admit it hired anyone.
A corp fixer offers deniable work with a very precise deadline.
The client is one of the Twelve. The cut-out won’t say which, and the pay says it doesn’t matter — unless the badge is an AEQ seal, in which case it was never a private hire.

name: a Greenline Ranger officer (Verdant Provision)
meet: the Greenline forward post at Cinderhold
pays: ¥ plus seed, water-tech, or ammunition off the books
pitch: A Greenline officer needs eyes past the wall that Verdant won’t sign off on.
The Rangers have a problem past the wall they can’t be seen handling.
Verdant wants a problem handled quietly before it reaches the corporate reports.

name: Ranger-Captain Cael Marrow, “the Gate”
pays: ¥ the settlement scraped together, and standing at the gate
pitch: Marrow doesn’t ask twice: Cinderhold needs something done and he trusts the crew to do it.
Marrow has read something in the ground he doesn’t like, and he needs proof.
Kestrel’s Clean Route is creeping closer, and Marrow needs the crew for something it can’t see.

name: Warden Krael, “the Landlord”
meet: his facilities office on the Grid
pays: ¥ and a blind eye on one SIN flag
pitch: Krael needs a problem on his levels solved without it touching his license.
The Landlord wants a rival warden embarrassed — or worse.
Krael is being squeezed from above and wants leverage of his own.

name: The Ferryman
meet: the last controlled crossing down to the Sinks
pitch: The Ferryman has a job past his crossings that he won’t touch himself.
Something below has stopped answering the Ferryman, and he wants to know why.
The Ferryman offers the toll waived for a job no one else will take.

name: The Choirmother
meet: the back room of her soup kitchen
pays: what her flock can gather, plus sanctuary on her block
pitch: The Choirmother asks, gently, for help protecting her people.
Something threatens her block, and the Choirmother is afraid of who is behind it.
The Choirmother says the Light sent the crew to her door.
